description: One slope written four ways and solved back from any of them — rise in 12, angle in degrees, grade in percent and the slope factor — plus the ridge height and the common rafter length once a span is typed. Estimate only; confirm with your plans, supplier and local code.

angle.description: Angle. Unit: degrees. Shown on the site only when "mode=angle" is set.

grade.description: Grade. Unit: %. Shown on the site only when "mode=grade" is set.

overhang.description: Overhang. Unit: in (imperial) or cm (metric). A number in that unit, or a string that carries its own unit such as "20 ft 6 in". Optional. measured horizontally, the way a framing square reads it.

rise.description: Rise. Unit: in (imperial) or cm (metric). A number in that unit, or a string that carries its own unit such as "20 ft 6 in". Default in metric: 15.24. how far the roof climbs over the run below. Holding a level on the roof: the drop measured at its far end.

run.description: Run. Unit: in (imperial) or cm (metric). A number in that unit, or a string that carries its own unit such as "20 ft 6 in". Default in metric: 30.48. the run your rise is measured over — 12 in is the convention, a 24 in level reads over 24.

span.description: Building span. Unit: ft (imperial) or m (metric). A number in that unit, or a string that carries its own unit such as "20 ft 6 in". Optional. wall to wall, if you want a rafter length. A common rafter runs over half of it.

system.description: Unit system the inputs are typed in and the defaults are taken from.
